findings.title: Async forEach means reschedule cleanup is not awaited
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` is not awaited and `forEach` ignores the returned promises. The callback now awaits `getCalendar` before calling `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting`, so the mutation continues to send the reschedule email and webhooks and returns while calendar/video cancellation has only started. In a serverless environment that work can be lost entirely, and failures become unhandled rejections. Use `for...of` with `await` or `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))`.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation API deletes are pushed after Promise.all
findings.body: In the recurring-booking branch, calendar cancellations are performed inside `forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` without awaiting the callback. After adding `await getCalendar(credential)`, the callback yields before pushing into `apiDeletes`; the later `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` therefore sees an empty `apiDeletes` and returns without waiting for those calendar deletions. Recurring calendar events may never be cancelled before the handler finishes. Collect promises with `await Promise.all(...)` or use a `for...of` loop.

findings.title: Reschedule calendar/video deletion races because async forEach is unawaited
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` is not awaited. The newly added `await getCalendar(...)` yields before `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` is even called, so `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` and the function return happen while the original calendar/video event may still be present. Any rejection from `getCalendar` or the delete calls is also an unhandled rejection instead of being caught by the surrounding `try/catch`. Use `for...of` or `await Promise.all(...)`.

findings.title: Reschedule cleanup starts after the response because async forEach is unawaited
findings.body: The callback passed to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach` is now `async` and contains `await getCalendar(...)`, but `forEach` does not wait for it. Calendar/video cancellation can therefore start after `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` has run and after the function has returned; failures are unhandled. This is the same unsafe pattern as in the Vital reschedule flow and should be converted to `for...of`/`Promise.all`.

findings.title: Dynamic imports are eagerly started for every app
findings.body: Each `import("./...")` in the object literal is evaluated as soon as this module is loaded, so all app modules start loading immediately. This does not provide lazy loading and may keep the same startup cost as the previous static imports. If the intent is to load app modules only when used, store loader functions such as `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")` and call the loader at the use site.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns promises in its calendar field
findings.body: `getCalendarCredentials` remains synchronous, but `getCalendar` is now async. As a result the exported helper returns objects whose `calendar` property is `Promise<Calendar | null>` instead of `Calendar | null`. `getConnectedCalendars` in this file awaits it, but any other exported consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` that treats `calendar` as a Calendar will break at runtime or type-check time. Either make `getCalendarCredentials` async and resolve all calendars, or update the type/contract and every caller.
